review.fixture_dtype_analysis: Under the usual float32 default dtype, multiplying boolean masks by Python floats constructs float32 shifts. Adding those shifts to float64 utilities preserves their already-rounded constants, whereas the expected expression applies the constants directly to float64 masses. Rounding of 1.3 and -0.7 can therefore explain an aggregate discrepancy on the observed approximately 4.4e-8 scale. Casting each mask to u.dtype before multiplication removes this precision mismatch without changing the intended fold shifts. This is a source-supported repair, not proof that the corrected canary passes; numerical execution remains required.
review.unchanged_mechanism_and_thresholds: The supplied before/after canary differs only in shift construction precision and shift_dtype report metadata. All eight checks, the 2e-9 default tolerance, other tolerances, seed, finite-difference steps and budget remain unchanged. The supplied mechanism sources are unchanged. No assertion is removed or weakened. This assessment is based on supplied text; hashes and runtime behavior were not independently verified.
review.screen_interpretation: The interpretation correctly preserves both outcomes: centered_full has the highest observed Macro-F1 and passes all four specified Macro comparisons, but fails the joint gate because CE exceeds centered_native by 0.024574354289782274. Its Macro-F1 gain over full is 0.005518254545902816, approximately 9.35% relative. Accuracy also declines against centered_native, although accuracy is not part of the implemented gate. The no-promotion decision is consistent with the code. A single initialization on a repeatedly explored development partition supports a descriptive positive lead, not statistical confirmation, causal mechanism attribution, full-data evidence or L5 acceptance.
